name: Example: Expressing the Maclaurin Series of a Function in Sigma Notation
problem:
Express the Maclaurin series expansion for $\cos{x},$ given by

$$
\cos{x} = 1 - \frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{x^4}{4!}- \frac{x^6}{6!}+\cdots ,
$$

using sigma notation.
worked_solution:
The first four terms of the series are

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =1 \\ {a}_{1} & =-\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{2} \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{{x}^{4}}{4!} \\ {a}_{3} & =-\frac{{x}^{6}}{6!}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we can express these terms using a common format, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{(-1)^{0}{x}^{2\cdot 0}}{(2\cdot 0)!} \\ {a}_{1} & =\frac{(-1)^{1}{x}^{2\cdot 1}}{(2\cdot 1)!} \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{(-1)^{2}{x}^{2\cdot 2}}{(2\cdot 2)!} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{(-1)^{3}{x}^{2\cdot 3}}{(2\cdot 3)!}.\end{aligned}
$$

We deduce that the general formula for the $n$th term is

$$
a_n = \dfrac{(-1)^n x^{2n}}{(2n)!} \,.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & ={\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{2n}}{(2n)!}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
